key_insight: SAGE-PINN removes cylindrical-axis singularities by encoding axisymmetric physics into the variables and network structure, enabling stable PINN simulation of coupled flow and heat transfer without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more practical for biomedical and other cylindrical multiphysics problems, especially when accurate conservation and boundary enforcement are critical.
method: Use the parity-preserving transform s = r^2 to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Encode mass conservation with a modified stream-function representation.
Apply boundary-fitted analytical ansätze plus staged momentum-thermal training, residual normalization, and parameter continuation for stability.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against finite-element references for stenosed-artery nanofluid flow, achieving single-precision mass conservation and about 1.6% axial-velocity error and 9.1% temperature error in the central operating range.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades near strongly buoyancy-dominated slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so these regimes may need extra tuning or stronger stabilization.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
